author: Maharishi Parashara
text: If the Lagnesha is in the 1st house itself, the native will be endowed with physical happiness, constitutional strength, natural valor, leadership, and independence. The native will be steadfast in resolve and achieve self-made fortune through personal enterprise.

author: Maharishi Parashara
text: The 2nd house governs accumulated liquid assets, speech, family legacy, and early nourishment. When the 2nd lord combines with benefic planets or occupies the 11th house, the native generates wealth from diverse streams and enjoys honor in society.

author: Maharishi Parashara
text: The 10th house is the zenith of the zodiac, governing vocation, societal authority, reputation, and public service. A strong 10th lord in a Kendra (1, 4, 7, 10) or Trikona (5, 9) confers enduring occupational stability, royal/governmental recognition, and high administrative status.

author: Maharishi Parashara
text: During the Mahadasha of a planet, results manifest in accordance with its natural significations (Karakatva), its functional house rulership, and its sthiti (dignity and placement). Benefics ruling Kendras and Trikonas produce prosperity and renown, while malefic lords require spiritual discipline, mindful action, and constructive remedies.

author: Maharishi Parashara
text: The Kendras are the houses of Lord Vishnu (effort, sustenance, structure) and the Trikonas are the houses of Goddess Lakshmi (grace, fortune, wisdom). The combination, mutual aspect, or parivartana (exchange) of a Kendra lord and a Trikona lord forms an exalted Raja Yoga, elevating the native to professional prominence regardless of birth circumstance.

author: Maharishi Parashara
text: Planetary afflictions and challenging dasha periods are neutralized through conscious behavioral discipline (samyama), recitation of sacred vibrations (Gayatri and Beej mantras), charitable service (dana to those in need), and fostering psychological virtues aligned with the afflicted graha.
